messages:
Maya: Heads up — preflight for the midnight deploy (service-runtime v2.3.4 -> v2.4.0) shows a warning on the artifact pin step, can someone confirm whether we should proceed with FF ramp or soft-hold?
Owen: I saw that too. The artifact upload is fine but CI labeler flagged a checksum mismatch for the optional chunked-kernel. not fatal, but worth pinning the canary artifact.
deploybot: deploy preflight for job deploy/service-runtime/2026-03-21-00:00 passed with warnings: [artifact-pin-warning]. To apply softhold: `@deploybot softhold on`  — to abort: `@deploybot abort`.
Jorge: My take — pin the canary to v2.4.0-canary-20260321, run canary at 1%/5%/25% ramp over 45m, monitor error-rate and p95 latency. If any rollback trigger hits, we softhold then drain cohorts.
sre-oncall: Agree with Jorge. Add explicit rollback thresholds: >1.0% user-error-rate OR +200ms p95 over baseline sustained for 2 consecutive 5m windows -> softhold. Also if model-routing errors spike >0.5% -> immediate rollback.
Product Ops: We need to ensure experiments are paused during the ramp so users don't get A/B noise. Can Product Ops pause the related experiments?
Product Ops: Paused experiment cohort X and Y. Also flagged the downstream telemetry dashboard with a short note. :white_check_mark:
Maya: Ok plan: 00:00 start canary artifact pinned to v2.4.0-canary-20260321 at 1% for 10m, then 5% for 15m, then 25% for 20m. Timestamps aligned to deploybot. If all green at 25% after 45m, we unpin and shift full traffic.
Owen: For the artifact pin action use this helper:```
rbctl artifacts pin --service service-runtime --version v2.4.0-canary-20260321 --reason "checksum warning; canary pin"
```
Maya: Noted. Also toggle plan for feature flag session-affinity-v2: start disabled, enable at 1% after canary is healthy. Ramp the flag independently with the same thresholds.
deploybot: acknowledged. Scheduled canary job deploy/service-runtime/2026-03-21-00:00 pinned -> v2.4.0-canary-20260321. Softhold command available.
sre-oncall: Quick checklist for watchers: 1) p95 latency dashboard (svc-runtime), 2) 5xx rate + user error rate, 3) queue depth on GPU-hosts, 4) model-cache miss ratio. If any of these cross thresholds, post here and call for softhold.
Jorge: We'll also enable prefix/KV cache diagnostics for the canary cohort to catch staggers. Added a lightweight eval set to check semantic regressions.
Maya: If we need to softhold, what's the exact flow? I want wording for runbook to paste:
Owen: Flow: 1) `@deploybot softhold on` -> stops further ramp steps and pins current cohort. 2) `rbctl route set --cohort drain --pct 0.0` to start draining new sessions. 3) If stable after 10m, `@deploybot resume` will continue ramp at previous rate. 4) If unstable, `@deploybot abort` to roll back to v2.3.4 and unpin.
Maya: Perfect. I'll paste this into the release notes. Also adding a short note: "Rollback triggers: sustained error or latency spikes as above; opt for softhold first to give ops time to triage."
deploybot: INFO: softhold available. To simulate health-check fail locally: `rbctl health simulate --service service-runtime --type p95-latency --delta 250ms`.
Product Ops: Added release note snippet and updated the change window to include a 15m buffer after ramp for post-deploy checks.
Maya: Alright team — starting the pinned canary at 00:00. Watchers: @sre-oncall, @Jorge, @Owen, please keep an eye. Post any anomalies here and we'll decide softhold vs abort. :rocket:
